line: Anything good planned for the weekend?
followUps: What are you most looking forward to about it?
Is that a regular thing for you, or a one-off?
shareBack: Mention one small plan of your own in a sentence, then ask something else about theirs.

line: This week has flown by. I can't tell yet if that's a good sign.
followUps: Has yours been more busy or more interesting?
What took up most of it?
shareBack: Offer the one thing that ate your week, briefly, then ask what they have left before Friday.
deliveryCue: Say it lightly, as a remark, and leave a pause.

line: What's been the best part of your week so far?
followUps: What made that one stand out?
Is there more of that coming up?
shareBack: Offer your own best moment of the week in one sentence, then hand it back with a question.

line: I'm still working out where to eat around here. Have you found anywhere good for lunch?
followUps: What do you usually order there?
Is it quick enough for a workday?
shareBack: Mention one place you've tried and what you thought, then ask if they know it.

line: While we wait for the others: where are you joining from today?
followUps: Is that your usual spot for calls?
What's it like there today?
shareBack: Say where you are and one detail about it, such as the view or the noise, then ask about theirs.
deliveryCue: Use in the first minute, before the call fills up.

line: Have you watched or read anything good lately? I need something new.
followUps: What did you like about it?
How did you come across it?
shareBack: Name one thing you enjoyed recently and why, in a sentence, then ask if it sounds like their kind of thing.

line: That last session gave me a lot to think about. What did you make of it?
followUps: Which part will you actually use?
Did anything in it surprise you?
shareBack: Offer the one point that stuck with you, then ask whether they saw it the same way.

line: Which session are you most looking forward to today?
followUps: What are you hoping to get out of it?
Have you heard that speaker before?
shareBack: Say which session you picked and why, briefly, then ask what else is on their list.

line: This place was a good pick. Have you been here before?
followUps: What would you recommend?
What's your usual kind of place for a night out?
shareBack: Mention a place you like for evenings like this, in a sentence, then ask if they know it.

line: I can't decide what to order. Does anything look good to you?
followUps: Are you an order-the-same-thing person or do you try new things?
What's the best thing you've eaten lately?
shareBack: Say what you're leaning toward and why, then ask what they'd pick between your two options.

line: Do you have any time off coming up?
followUps: What's the plan for it?
Are you a plan-everything person or a see-what-happens person?
shareBack: Mention your next break, or the one you wish you had, in a sentence, then ask for a tip.

line: Before we start: anything fun on your calendar this week, outside of meetings?
followUps: How did that come about?
Is that something you do often?
shareBack: Offer one thing you have on this week that isn't work, then ask a follow-up about theirs.
deliveryCue: Good for the minute or two before the agenda starts.

line: How was the trip in? Did you have far to come?
followUps: How do you usually pass the time on that trip?
Are you heading straight back afterwards or staying a while?
shareBack: Say how your own trip in went, in a sentence, then ask about the rest of their day.

line: Do you have a go-to coffee order, or do you change it up?
followUps: Where's the best one you've had around here?
Is that a morning-only thing or all day?
shareBack: Admit your own order, however plain, then ask where they'd send you for a good one.

line: I think we're the first ones on. Nice to have a minute before it gets going.
followUps: Has today been back-to-back calls for you?
Anything good planned once you log off?
shareBack: Mention how your day has gone in a few words, then ask what's left on theirs.
deliveryCue: Say it as a remark and let them pick it up.

line: Settle something for me: what's the best snack in the office kitchen?
followUps: What's the one that should never be restocked?
Do you bring lunch in or go out for it?
shareBack: Give your own pick and defend it in a sentence, then ask what they'd add to the shelf.
deliveryCue: Keep it playful.

line: I tried cooking something new over the weekend and it mostly worked. Do you have a dish you always fall back on?
followUps: Who taught you that one?
What's the trick to getting it right?
shareBack: Add one detail about what went wrong with yours, then ask what they'd cook for guests.

line: What's keeping your team busy right now?
followUps: Which part of that are you enjoying?
When does it ease off?
shareBack: Name the one thing taking most of your own time, in a sentence, then ask what comes after theirs.

line: What's next for your team once this project is done?
followUps: Is that something you're looking forward to?
How did that end up on your plate?
shareBack: Mention what your own team turns to next, briefly, then ask what they'd choose if it were up to them.

line: That was a clear presentation. The example in the middle really landed. How did you come up with it?
followUps: How long did it take to get it that tight?
What did you cut that you wish you'd kept?
shareBack: Say which point you'll use yourself and how, then ask what they'd change next time.
deliveryCue: Name the specific part you liked; it should be true.

line: Good to meet you today. I enjoyed hearing about what you're working on.
followUps: How did the rest of your day go?
Would you be up for a coffee sometime to hear more?
shareBack: If they reply, mention one thing they said that stuck with you, then leave the next step open.
deliveryCue: Send the same day. It needs no reply.

line: Saw this and thought of what you said in the meeting. No need to reply.
followUps: Does it match what you've been seeing?
Have you come across anything else good on this?
shareBack: If they reply, say in one line what you took from it, then ask what they think.
deliveryCue: Attach the article or link. Only send something they'd really want.

line: Heading out for coffee in ten. Want anything, or want to come along?
followUps: How's your morning been so far?
Do you have a favorite place nearby?
shareBack: On the walk, mention one thing from your morning, then ask about theirs.

line: Thanks for today. The way you explained that made it click for me. Did it go how you hoped?
followUps: What would you do differently next time?
What's the next step from your side?
shareBack: Say in one line what you'll do with what they explained, then leave it there.
deliveryCue: Be specific about what helped. A yes-or-no reply is fine.

line: Are you in the office tomorrow? I'm in and would be glad of lunch company.
followUps: Is there somewhere you've been wanting to try?
What time suits you?
shareBack: At lunch, offer one thing about your week first, then ask what theirs has been like.

line: Hope the trip back was easy. It was good to see you this week.
followUps: Did you get home at a reasonable hour?
Is next week a quieter one for you?
shareBack: If they reply, mention one moment from the visit you enjoyed, then wish them a good weekend.
deliveryCue: Needs no reply; a thumbs-up is a fine answer.

line: It's been a while. I walked past the place where we had lunch and thought of you. Hope things are going well.
followUps: Would a quick coffee or call sometime suit you?
What's been keeping you busy lately?
shareBack: If they reply, give one line on what you've been up to, then ask an easy question about them.
deliveryCue: Swap in your own real reminder. Ask for nothing.

line: No need for a long reply. Just checking the first week has gone smoothly on your side.
followUps: Is there anything that would make next week easier?
Would a quick call be useful, or is a message fine?
shareBack: If they reply, share one thing you noticed going well from your side, then ask if they agree.
deliveryCue: Change "first week" to whatever just happened.

line: Congratulations on the launch. I saw the announcement and it looked great. Is the team getting a breather now?
followUps: Which part are you proudest of?
What comes next?
shareBack: Say which detail of it you liked most, in one line, then leave the conversation open.
deliveryCue: Change "launch" to their real news.

line: That meeting ran long. Did you manage to get any lunch?
followUps: Want to grab something quick now?
Is the rest of your afternoon any calmer?
shareBack: Say how your own lunch plans survived, in a line, then suggest a real one another day.

line: Looking forward to seeing you on Thursday. Is there anything you'd like me to bring or prepare?
followUps: Who else from your side will be there?
Would you like to get lunch after?
shareBack: Mention the one thing you're hoping to cover, in a line, then ask if that fits their plan.
deliveryCue: Change the day. A one-word reply is enough.

line: You seemed a little flat after that meeting. No need to reply. I'm around if you want to talk it over.
followUps: Do you want to talk it through, or would a distraction be better?
What would help most right now?
shareBack: If they open up, listen first; later, mention a time a meeting left you feeling the same.
deliveryCue: Only if you saw it, and you know them well. Don't push.

line: What are you working on right now that you're actually enjoying?
followUps: What is it about that one that you like?
How did you end up with it?
shareBack: Name the piece of your own work you're enjoying most, in a sentence, then ask what they'd like more of.

line: What's something you've picked up this year that's made the job easier?
followUps: How did you come across that?
What were you doing before you found it?
shareBack: Offer one small trick or habit that helped you, then ask whether they've tried anything like it.

line: Your meetings always finish on time and still get somewhere. How do you do it?
followUps: What do you do when someone goes off track?
Did you learn that from someone, or work it out?
shareBack: Admit one thing you find hard about running meetings, then ask what they'd try in your place.
deliveryCue: Only say it if it's true of them.

line: I have a tricky email to write and you're good at these. How would you open it?
followUps: What would you leave out?
Has one of these ever gone badly for you?
shareBack: Say what you were planning to write, briefly, then ask what they'd change.
deliveryCue: Ask only when they have a few minutes.

line: Seems like that project has a lot of moving parts right now.
followUps: Which part is taking most of your attention?
Is any of it fun, or is it all juggling?
shareBack: Mention a time you had something similar on your plate, in a sentence, then ask what would help.
deliveryCue: Only if it's true. Say it as an observation and wait.

line: What's been on your mind most this week, work or otherwise?
followUps: What's making that one stick?
Is it a good kind of busy or the other kind?
shareBack: Offer the one thing you keep coming back to this week, briefly, then return to theirs.
deliveryCue: Give them time; let them choose how much to say.

line: Is there anything you'd like to be doing more of at work next year?
followUps: What draws you to that?
What would need to change for it to happen?
shareBack: Name one thing you'd like more of yourself, in a sentence, then ask how you could help with theirs.

line: Do you see yourself staying on this path, or is something else starting to pull at you?
followUps: How long has that been on your mind?
What would the first small step look like?
shareBack: Share where you honestly stand on your own path, in a sentence or two, then go back to theirs.
deliveryCue: For a private moment. Listen; don't steer.

line: I was thinking about that project we nearly didn't finish. What do you remember most about it?
followUps: Would you do it the same way again?
What did you take from it that you still use?
shareBack: Offer the one moment you remember best, in a sentence, then ask if they saw it the same way.

line: What's the strangest job you had before this one?
followUps: What was the best part of it?
Did anything from it turn out to be useful here?
shareBack: Tell your own oddest job in one sentence, with one detail, then ask for the rest of their story.
deliveryCue: Best over food or a drink.

line: What do you like to do to switch off after a week like this one?
followUps: How did you get into that?
Do you get to do it as often as you'd like?
shareBack: Mention the one thing that helps you switch off, in a sentence, then ask what they'd recommend trying.

line: Since we have the drive: what's the best work trip you've ever been on?
followUps: What made that one so good?
Is there a place you'd go back to on your own time?
shareBack: Offer your own best or worst work trip in a sentence, then ask where they'd like to be sent next.

line: Looking back, which call you made here taught you the most?
followUps: What do you know now that you didn't then?
Has it changed how you decide things?
shareBack: Share one decision of your own that taught you something, briefly, then ask what they would tell someone facing it.
deliveryCue: Best in a private moment. Listen; don't fix.

line: You've been here longer than I have. What do you wish someone had told you in your first year?
followUps: How did you find that out in the end?
Who helped you most back then?
shareBack: Mention one thing you're still figuring out here, then ask what they'd do in your position.

line: Last time you mentioned things were about to get busy. How did that turn out?
followUps: What was the hardest part of it?
Is it settling down now?
shareBack: Offer a short update on what you mentioned last time too, then ask what's next for them.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real thing they told you last time.

line: What's gone better than you expected this year?
followUps: What do you think made the difference?
Did it change your plans for next year?
shareBack: Name one thing that surprised you on the upside, in a sentence, then ask what they're hoping for next.

line: What are you most excited about for the team over the next few months?
followUps: What would make that go really well?
Where do you think we can help most?
shareBack: Mention the piece of upcoming work you're most looking forward to, in a sentence, then ask how it fits their plans.

line: I was curious how you landed on the new priorities. What tipped it for you?
followUps: What was the hardest thing to leave off the list?
How do you test a decision like that before you commit?
shareBack: Say which priority makes most sense from where you sit, then ask what they'd like your team to keep in mind.
deliveryCue: Sound curious, not challenging.

line: You've handled a lot of difficult conversations. Any advice for someone with one coming up?
followUps: What do you do in the first minute?
Is there one that taught you the most?
shareBack: Describe your upcoming conversation in a sentence, without names, then ask what they'd watch for.

line: I enjoyed your talk earlier, especially the story at the start. How do you prepare for those?
followUps: How do you decide what to leave out?
Does it get easier the more of them you do?
shareBack: Mention the one point you'll take back to your own work, then ask what they'd add with more time.
deliveryCue: Name the part you really liked.

line: What are you reading or listening to lately that's been worth the time?
followUps: What's the main thing you took from it?
How do you find the good ones?
shareBack: Name one thing you've read or heard recently and one idea from it, then ask if they've come across it.

line: What's something you learned early in your career that you still use?
followUps: Who did you learn that from?
When has it mattered most?
shareBack: Offer one lesson you've picked up recently, in a sentence, then ask if it matches their experience.

line: I'd like to get better at presenting to senior people. What do you notice in the ones who do it well?
followUps: What's the most common mistake you see?
How should I open if I only have five minutes?
shareBack: Mention one thing you already do when presenting, then ask whether they'd keep it or drop it.

line: What's the part of the job you enjoy most these days?
followUps: Has that changed over the years?
What would you like more time for?
shareBack: Name the part of your own work you enjoy most, in a sentence, then ask a follow-up about theirs.

line: It feels like the team has found its rhythm this quarter.
followUps: What do you think made the difference?
What would you like us to keep doing?
shareBack: Offer one specific thing you've noticed working better, then ask whether they see it the same way.
deliveryCue: Only say it if you believe it.

line: How did you first get into this field?
followUps: What kept you in it?
Was there a turning point along the way?
shareBack: Give your own route in, in one sentence with one detail, then ask what they'd tell someone starting now.

line: Do you get much chance to come to these, or is tonight a rare one?
followUps: What's the best one you've been to?
Who else should I make sure to meet while I'm here?
shareBack: Say how often you make it to events like this, in a sentence, then ask what they're hoping to get from it.

line: I'm looking for a good book on leading a team. Is there one you'd recommend?
followUps: What did you take from it?
Is there one you'd tell people to skip?
shareBack: Mention the last useful thing you read, in a sentence, then ask if it's worth your time to go further.

line: What do you pay attention to when you want to know how things are really going?
followUps: How did you learn to look for that?
What do people tend to miss?
shareBack: Say what you tend to watch in your own work, briefly, then ask what else you should be noticing.

line: I thought delaying the launch was the right call. What made you confident about it?
followUps: What would have changed your mind?
How did you bring everyone along?
shareBack: Say what the decision made easier for you, in a sentence, then ask what they're watching next.
deliveryCue: Swap in a real decision you agreed with.

line: I've been trying to block out time for focused work, with mixed results. How do you protect yours?
followUps: What do you say no to?
Has that changed as your role has grown?
shareBack: Add what has and hasn't worked for you, in a sentence, then ask which of their habits to try first.

line: Thanks for making time for this. I know this week is a packed one.
followUps: Does it ease up after this week?
What's the main thing on your plate right now?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what you're hoping to get from the time, then ask what would be most useful to them.
deliveryCue: Say it warmly, then pause before the agenda.

line: Is this your first time in the city, or do you know it well?
followUps: What have you managed to see so far?
Is there anything you'd like to fit in before you leave?
shareBack: Suggest one place you like nearby, in a sentence, then ask what kind of thing they enjoy.
deliveryCue: Use when they have traveled to you.

line: I've heard good things about your team from everyone who's worked with them. What's the secret?
followUps: How did you build that?
What do you look for when someone new joins?
shareBack: Mention one specific thing you've seen their team do well, then ask how they keep it up.
deliveryCue: Only if you have really heard it.

line: You know this market far better than I do. What should I be reading to keep up?
followUps: What's changed most in the last year or two?
Who do you think gets it right?
shareBack: Say what you currently follow, in a sentence, then ask whether it's giving you the right picture.

line: Is there a local dish or a place I should try while I'm in town?
followUps: What do you order there?
Where would you take a visitor for one good meal?
shareBack: Mention the best thing you've eaten on the trip so far, then ask if they'd agree with the choice.
deliveryCue: Use when you are the visitor.

line: How did your company get started on this? I'd like to hear the story behind it.
followUps: What was the hardest part early on?
What surprised you most along the way?
shareBack: Say what first caught your attention about their work, in a sentence, then ask what's next for it.

line: It sounds like this has been a big year for your team.
followUps: What are you proudest of from it?
What made it possible?
shareBack: Mention the one piece of their year you noticed from outside, then ask what they're aiming at next.
deliveryCue: Say it as an observation and let them fill in the rest.

line: Good to see you. Is today a busy one or a quiet one?
followUps: What's taking up most of it?
Anything good at the end of it?
shareBack: Say in a few words what your own day looks like, then wish them luck with theirs.
deliveryCue: For the elevator or the hallway. A short answer is fine.

line: Whatever you're heating up smells a lot better than my lunch.
followUps: Is that a recipe of yours?
Do you usually bring lunch in?
shareBack: Admit what you brought today, in a few words, then ask for one easy lunch idea.
deliveryCue: Say it lightly by the microwave and leave it there if they're in a hurry.

line: I'm grabbing a coffee before this starts. Can I get you one?
followUps: How do you take it?
Is this your first meeting of the day or one of many?
shareBack: On the way back, mention how your morning has gone in a line, then ask what's left on theirs.

line: Thanks for the quick turnaround on this. It made my afternoon a lot easier.
followUps: Was it a pain to pull together?
Is there anything you need back from me?
shareBack: If they reply, say in one line what it let you do, then leave it there.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real thing they did.

line: Nice work in that meeting. You handled the tough question really well.
followUps: Did you see it coming?
How did you decide what to say?
shareBack: Say in one line what you took from how they handled it, then leave it there.
deliveryCue: Name the real moment. Only say it if it's true.

line: Hope the rest of your afternoon is a quieter one.
followUps: Anything good waiting at the end of the day?
Is tomorrow any calmer?
shareBack: If they answer, mention one small thing you're looking forward to tonight, then wish them a good evening.
deliveryCue: Needs no reply.

line: Long day, or just getting started?
followUps: What's the big thing on today's list?
Anything fun after work?
shareBack: Say where your own day stands in a few words, then wish them a good one.
deliveryCue: Good for an elevator ride or a coffee line.

line: Just saw your note. Thanks, this is exactly what I needed.
followUps: Do you want me to flag anything back to you?
Was this one easy to track down?
shareBack: If they reply, say in a line what you'll do with it next, then leave it there.
deliveryCue: Needs no reply.

line: Who's up for a coffee run in ten minutes?
followUps: Where should we go?
Does anyone want something brought back?
shareBack: On the walk, mention one thing from your morning, then ask someone about theirs.

line: While we wait for a few more people: does anyone have a good recommendation for the weekend?
followUps: Have you been there yourself?
What should someone order or see first?
shareBack: Offer one place or thing you liked recently, in a sentence, then ask who else has one.
deliveryCue: For the first minute of a call or meeting, before it fills up.

line: What's everyone ordering? I need someone to decide for me.
followUps: Is that what you always get here?
Anyone tried the special?
shareBack: Say what you're torn between, then ask the table to settle it.
deliveryCue: For a team lunch, as the menus come out.

line: What took up most of your time this week, and was it the stuff you wanted to be doing?
followUps: What would you rather have spent it on?
What got in the way?
shareBack: Name the part of your own week that went sideways, briefly, then ask what would help next week.

line: If you could hand one thing on your plate to someone else, what would it be?
followUps: What makes that one the drag?
Is there a way we could make it lighter?
shareBack: Admit the one task you'd hand off yourself, in a sentence, then come back to theirs.
deliveryCue: Ask it lightly; it's an invitation, not a test.

line: On a scale from calm to chaos, where is this week landing for you?
followUps: What tipped it that way?
What would move it one notch calmer?
shareBack: Say where your own week lands, in a few words, then ask what would help theirs.

line: Before we get into the project: anything this week that went better or worse than you expected?
followUps: What do you think made the difference?
Is there anything I should know about it?
shareBack: Share one thing from your own week that surprised you, briefly, then ask what they need from you.
deliveryCue: For the start of a 1:1. Let them choose which one to answer.

line: Is there anything I could take off your plate or clear out of your way this week?
followUps: What's the thing slowing you down most?
Who should I talk to about it?
shareBack: Say in a line what you can actually do by when, then ask if that would help.
deliveryCue: Only offer what you can really do.

line: What's one thing that would make next week easier for you?
followUps: Is that something I can help with?
What's been making it hard?
shareBack: Mention one thing you're changing about your own next week, briefly, then ask how you can help with theirs.

line: You said it's all good, and I believe you. If one thing were a little less good, what would it be?
followUps: How long has that been going on?
What would make it better?
shareBack: If they open up, thank them, then say what you'll do about it and when.
deliveryCue: For a 1:1 that keeps getting "all good". Say it lightly, then wait.

line: No need to reply right away. Is there anything you're waiting on from me?
followUps: When do you need it by?
Is anything else stuck?
shareBack: If they name something, say in a line when you'll have it done, then thank them for flagging it.

line: I want to learn how you like to work. Do you prefer quick check-ins, or fewer and longer ones?
followUps: What's worked best with past managers?
How do you like to get feedback?
shareBack: Say in a sentence how you like to work, then ask what you should know about them.
deliveryCue: Good for the first weeks of managing someone.

line: What's one thing about how this team works that you'd keep exactly as it is?
followUps: What makes it work?
Is there one thing you'd change?
shareBack: Name the thing you'd protect yourself, in a sentence, then ask what they'd change.

line: I can take something off your list this week. What would help most?
followUps: Would it help if I took the next update?
Is there anyone I should talk to for you?
shareBack: If they can't think of anything, offer one concrete task you could take, then let them decide.
deliveryCue: Offer one specific thing if they can't think of any.

line: I can cover that for you if it would help. Just say the word.
followUps: When would you need it by?
Is there anything else I should know about it?
shareBack: Keep the focus on them. If they say yes, confirm what you'll do and when, in a line.
deliveryCue: Name the real task. Only offer what you can do.

line: That meeting was a tough one, and you held your ground well. Want to talk it through, or leave it till tomorrow?
followUps: Which part is still bugging you?
Is there anything I can do before the next one?
shareBack: Listen first. Later, if it helps, mention one meeting that rattled you too, in a sentence.
deliveryCue: Say it privately, soon after. Either answer is fine.

line: No need to go into it. I just wanted you to know I noticed, and I'm around.
followUps: Would a coffee help, or would you rather keep your head down today?
Is there anything I can take off your plate?
shareBack: Don't share your own story yet. If they talk, listen, then offer one specific thing you can do.
deliveryCue: Only if you've really noticed something. Don't press.

line: I heard things have been hard. I'm sorry. No need to reply.
followUps: Is there anything at work I can take off your hands?
Would a quiet coffee help sometime this week?
shareBack: If they reply, thank them and offer one specific thing, in a line. No advice.
deliveryCue: Send it once. Silence is a fine answer.

line: Do you feel like talking about it, or would a distraction be better?
followUps: What would help most right now?
Want me to just sit with you for a bit?
shareBack: Follow their lead. If they want a distraction, offer one light thing from your own week.
deliveryCue: Either answer is fine. Follow their lead.

line: That sounds really hard. I'm sorry you're dealing with it.
followUps: Do you want to talk about it, or would a break help more?
Is there anything at work I can take on?
shareBack: Leave room. If you speak again, offer one specific kind of help rather than your own story.
deliveryCue: Say it, then leave room. No need to fill the silence.

line: Want to take a walk and get out of here for ten minutes? We don't have to talk about it.
followUps: Coffee or just air?
Do you want company, or would some quiet be better?
shareBack: On the walk, let them lead. If they stay quiet, mention one small, light thing from your week.

line: Thinking of you today. Lunch is on me whenever you want it, no talking required.
followUps: What day works for you?
Anywhere you've been craving?
shareBack: At lunch, let them lead the talk. If they want distraction, offer a light story of your own.
deliveryCue: Needs no reply.

line: Take the time you need. Tell me which deadlines matter most and I'll move the rest.
followUps: Is there anything you want me to tell the team, or keep quiet?
Who can pick up the urgent pieces?
shareBack: Keep the focus on them. Say in a line what you'll handle and when you'll check back.
deliveryCue: Only promise what you can really move.

line: Congratulations on the promotion. It's well earned. What part of the new role are you most looking forward to?
followUps: When did you find out?
What do you want to do first?
shareBack: Say in a sentence one thing you've seen them do that shows why, then ask what they need to get started.
deliveryCue: Swap in their real news.

line: The launch went really well, and your part in it showed. What was the moment you knew it would work?
followUps: What was the hardest part to get right?
What would you do the same way next time?
shareBack: Name the specific piece of their work you noticed, in a line, then ask what's next for them.
deliveryCue: Name their real contribution.

line: I wanted to say it plainly: the way you handled that client call was excellent. How did you prepare for it?
followUps: Was there a moment you weren't sure about?
What would you tell someone new about calls like that?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what you'll borrow from how they did it, then hand it back.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real win. Be specific about what was good.

line: Just heard the news. Congratulations! This is a big one. How are you celebrating?
followUps: When does it start?
What are you most excited about?
shareBack: If they reply, say one thing you're glad about for them, in a line, then leave it open.
deliveryCue: Send it the same day you hear.

line: I heard about the award. Congratulations. What did it take to get there?
followUps: Who else on your team was part of it?
What's the next goal?
shareBack: Mention the detail that impressed you most, in a line, then ask what comes next.
deliveryCue: Swap in their real news.

line: Congratulations on the news. I saw the announcement. What does it mean for your team?
followUps: What's the first thing you'll do with it?
How long has it been in the works?
shareBack: Say what caught your eye in the announcement, in a line, then ask how you can help.
deliveryCue: Only if you've read it. Mention one real detail.

line: I saw the news about your team's launch. Congratulations. What was the hardest part to get right?
followUps: How is the team marking it?
What's next now that it's out?
shareBack: Name the piece of the launch you liked most, in a line, then ask what they're proudest of.
deliveryCue: Swap in their real launch.

line: Congratulations on the new role. The team's lucky to have you in it. What are you hoping to do first?
followUps: What surprised you about the move?
What will you miss from the old role?
shareBack: Say in a line what you're glad about from your side, then offer one way you can help.

line: Big week for this team. Congratulations, everyone. What was the hardest part to pull off?
followUps: Who saved the day at the last minute?
What should we do differently next time?
shareBack: Name one person's specific contribution, briefly, then ask who else deserves a shout-out.
deliveryCue: Swap in what the team actually pulled off.

line: There's cake in the kitchen for the launch. Come grab some before it disappears.
followUps: Who picked the flavor?
Anyone have a favorite moment from launch week?
shareBack: In the kitchen, thank one person for one specific thing, then ask how their week is going.

line: Can we take a minute to celebrate? This launch happened because of everyone in this room.
followUps: Who wants to tell the story of the night before it went out?
What are you proudest of?
shareBack: Thank one or two people for something specific, then hand the floor to the room.
deliveryCue: Say it at the start of a meeting, before the agenda.

line: Congratulations on the launch, everyone! What was your favorite moment from it?
followUps: Who else should we be thanking?
What's the first thing you're doing with the free time?
shareBack: Share your own favorite moment in a line, then ask who else deserves a thank-you.

line: Before we start: a quick thank-you to everyone who stayed late last week. It really paid off.
followUps: Did anyone get to catch up on sleep?
What made the difference in the end?
shareBack: Name one specific thing that went well, in a sentence, then move on to the agenda.
deliveryCue: Swap in what really happened. Keep it short.

line: Raise your coffee for the launch, everyone. What's the first thing you're doing with your free time?
followUps: Anyone taking a real day off?
What's been waiting the longest?
shareBack: Say what you're doing with yours in a line, then ask the quietest person what theirs is.
deliveryCue: Keep it light. Good at a team lunch or standup.

line: Want to grab lunch somewhere other than our desks this week? Thursday works for me.
followUps: Anywhere you've been wanting to try?
What time is good for you?
shareBack: At lunch, ask about their week first, then offer one thing from yours.
deliveryCue: Swap in a day you can really do.

line: There's a talk after work on Thursday that looks good. Want to go together? No pressure if you're swamped.
followUps: Have you heard the speaker before?
Want to grab food after?
shareBack: Say in a line what drew you to it, then ask what they hope to get out of it.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real event.

line: Coffee walk at three? I need a break from this screen.
followUps: Usual place or somewhere new?
How's your afternoon shaping up?
shareBack: On the walk, ask about their day first, then offer one thing from yours.

line: We keep saying we'll get a drink after work. Is this Friday the one?
followUps: Where should we go?
Want to ask anyone else along?
shareBack: If it's a no, offer one other date, then leave it with them.
deliveryCue: Leave an easy out. Coffee works just as well.

line: Want to grab a coffee after this and properly catch up?
followUps: How long have you got?
Anything you want to talk through?
shareBack: Over coffee, let them go first, then share one thing from your own week.
deliveryCue: Say it at the end of a meeting, on the way out.

line: I'm trying the new lunch place on Friday. Want to come along?
followUps: Have you heard anything about it?
What time suits you?
shareBack: At lunch, ask what they've been up to first, then offer one thing from yours.
deliveryCue: Swap in a real place nearby.

line: Could I get 20 minutes with you in the next couple of weeks? I'd like your advice on where to grow next.
followUps: What would be most useful for me to bring?
Is there a time that's usually quieter for you?
shareBack: In the meeting, say in two sentences where you think you could grow, then ask what they see.
deliveryCue: Make it easy to say "later": offer two time windows.

line: I'm hoping to meet someone on the product side. Would you be comfortable introducing me to anyone there?
followUps: Is there someone you think I should talk to first?
Would a short note from me make it easier?
shareBack: Say in one line why you want the intro, then offer to write a blurb they can forward.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real team. Say why in a line.

line: I'm applying for a new role and would be grateful if you'd be a reference. Would that work for you?
followUps: What would be helpful for me to send you?
Is there anything you'd want me to highlight?
shareBack: Send the job details and two or three things you'd like them to speak to, then thank them.
deliveryCue: Best for a former boss. Make no a comfortable answer.

line: It's been a while since we worked together. I'm weighing a career decision and would value 15 minutes of your thinking. Any chance?
followUps: Would a call or a coffee be easier?
Is next week too soon?
shareBack: If they say yes, send a two-line summary of the decision ahead of time, then thank them.
deliveryCue: For a former boss. Name the decision in a line if you can.

line: You've taken teams through changes like this before. When you have a moment, could I ask how you'd approach it?
followUps: What did you wish you'd known the first time?
What would you watch for early on?
shareBack: Describe your situation in two sentences, without names, then ask what they'd do first.

line: Do you have ten minutes after this? I'd like to get your take on something.
followUps: Is now good, or later today?
Would a quick call work better?
shareBack: When you meet, state the question in two sentences, then listen before adding more.
deliveryCue: Say it as the meeting ends. Let them pick the time.

line: Last time we spoke, you were about to start the new rollout. How did the first few weeks go?
followUps: What surprised you most?
Is there anything we could make easier?
shareBack: Share a short update on your side since you last talked, then ask what's next for them.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real thing they told you last time.

line: Good to see you again. Did the plan you mentioned last time work out?
followUps: What was the hardest part?
What's next for it?
shareBack: Offer a one-line update on what you were working on then, then ask a follow-up about theirs.
deliveryCue: Only if you remember the plan. Name it if you can.

line: I've been thinking about the problem you raised when we met. I have one idea, if a quick call would be useful.
followUps: Would this week or next suit you better?
Has anything changed since we talked?
shareBack: On the call, give the idea in two sentences, then ask how it fits what they're seeing.
deliveryCue: Only if you really have an idea worth their time.

line: Following up on our chat: I've attached the notes and the two options we discussed. Happy to talk through either.
followUps: Does one of the options look closer to what you need?
Is anyone else on your side who should see this?
shareBack: If they reply, say which option you'd lean toward and why, in a line, then ask what they think.
deliveryCue: Send within a day. Attach what you promised.

line: It's been a few months since we properly caught up. What's changed on your side since then?
followUps: What's taking most of your attention now?
Is there anything coming up we should plan for?
shareBack: Give a one-line update from your side, then ask which of their changes matters most.

line: Thanks for jumping on. Before we start, how did last week's event turn out?
followUps: What was the best part of it?
Would you do it again?
shareBack: Say in a line what you heard about it or how your own week went, then move to the agenda.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real thing they had going on.

line: Would it help to set up 30 minutes next week to go through the options? Tuesday or Wednesday both work for me.
followUps: Who else should be on it?
Is there anything you'd like me to prepare?
shareBack: Confirm the time in a line and say what you'll bring, then thank them.
deliveryCue: Swap in days you can really do.

line: Before we wrap up: what would be a useful next step from your side?
followUps: When would be a good time to pick it up again?
Who else should I loop in?
shareBack: Say what you'll do next and by when, in a sentence, then thank them for the time.
deliveryCue: For the last five minutes of a meeting.

line: I'll be near your office on the 12th. Would coffee be useful, or is a call easier?
followUps: Is there somewhere you like nearby?
Is there anything you'd want to cover?
shareBack: Say in a line what you'd like to hear about, then let them pick the format.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real date. Either answer is fine.

line: Should I send a short summary and a couple of times to follow up? Then you can pick what suits.
followUps: Is there anything you'd want in the summary?
Anyone else who should get it?
shareBack: Send it the same day, with two time options, and thank them for the time.

line: Thanks again for today. I'll send the proposal by Friday. Would a quick call the week after work for you?
followUps: Which days are easiest for you?
Is there anything you'd like me to include?
shareBack: If they reply, confirm the time in a line, then leave it there.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real deliverable and date.

line: I should get back to it, but I'm glad we talked about that. Good luck with the rest of the week.
followUps: When's the big deadline?
Will you tell me how it goes?
shareBack: Name one thing they said that you'll remember, in a few words, then go.
deliveryCue: Say it warmly as you stand up. Give the real reason you're leaving.

line: I'll let you get back to it. I want to hear how that turns out.
followUps: When will you know?
Want to grab coffee after?
shareBack: Mention the specific thing you want to hear about, in a few words, then wrap up.
deliveryCue: Name the thing they told you about.

line: I have to jump back into something, but this was a nice break. Talk soon.
followUps: Same time tomorrow?
Want me to send you that link?
shareBack: If they reply, end on one warm line about something they said, then sign off.

line: Good place to stop. Thanks, everyone. That was a useful hour.
followUps: Does anyone need anything before we go?
Same time next week?
shareBack: Name the one next step and who has it, in a sentence, then end on time.
deliveryCue: Say it a minute before the end, not after.

line: I'll let you get to your next meeting. Thanks, this was really useful.
followUps: Is there anything you need from me before next time?
Should I send a quick summary?
shareBack: Say in a line what you'll do with what you heard, then leave on time.
deliveryCue: Mention one thing that was useful if you can.

line: Thanks for the time today. I'll send notes by tomorrow.
followUps: Is there anyone else who should get them?
Anything you'd like me to add?
shareBack: Thank them for one specific thing they offered, then follow through on the notes.
deliveryCue: Only promise a time you can keep.

line: I'm sorry to see you go, and really glad for you. Where's the best place to stay in touch?
followUps: What are you most looking forward to in the new role?
When do you start?
shareBack: Say in a line one thing you'll miss about working with them, then wish them luck.
deliveryCue: For someone leaving the company.

line: I'll miss working with you. You set the bar for running a good meeting. What are you most looking forward to next?
followUps: What will you miss most from here?
Can I take you for a goodbye coffee before you go?
shareBack: Share one moment of working together you remember, in a sentence, then ask how to stay in touch.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real thing they did well.

line: Thank you for everything you taught me here. I hope I can still come to you for advice now and then.
followUps: What's the best way to reach you?
What are you most looking forward to?
shareBack: Name one lesson you'll keep using, in a sentence, then wish them well.
deliveryCue: For a boss who is leaving, or when you are.

line: I have to head back, but this was a good idea. Let's do it again next month.
followUps: Who wants to pick the place next time?
Same day work for everyone?
shareBack: Thank whoever set it up, in a line, then head out.
deliveryCue: For leaving a team lunch or coffee.

line: Going to miss having you on this team. Keep us posted on where you land, and come back for lunch sometime.
followUps: When's your last day?
What are you most excited about?
shareBack: Add one specific thing they did for the team, in a sentence, then wish them luck.
deliveryCue: For a coworker leaving. Works in a card or the team chat.

line: Before we let you go: what's one thing you hope this team keeps doing after you've left?
followUps: And one thing we should stop?
What will you miss most?
shareBack: Thank them for one specific thing, in a sentence, then let the room add theirs.
deliveryCue: For a farewell lunch or the last team meeting.

line: Signing off for the day. Thanks for the help on that one, everyone.
followUps: Anything you need from me first thing tomorrow?
Who's in the office tomorrow?
shareBack: If anyone replies, answer in a line and wish them a good evening.

line: Congratulations on the new role, and thanks for everything here. Make sure we have a way to reach you.
followUps: When's your last day?
What are you most looking forward to?
shareBack: Add one specific thing you'll remember, in a line, then wish them well.
deliveryCue: For a farewell thread or card.

line: That's all from me. Have a good weekend, everyone.
followUps: Anyone doing anything fun?
See you all Monday?
shareBack: If someone mentions a plan, ask one follow-up, then sign off.

line: What's something you're looking forward to this year, at work or outside it?
followUps: What's drawing you to that?
How long has it been on the list?
shareBack: Name one thing you're looking forward to, in a sentence, then ask what would make theirs go well.

line: Is there a skill you've been wanting to pick up lately?
followUps: What got you interested in it?
How would you start?
shareBack: Mention one thing you'd like to learn yourself, in a line, then ask how they'd go about theirs.

line: What's a tool or habit you couldn't do your job without?
followUps: How did you find it?
Would you recommend it to someone new?
shareBack: Offer one of your own in a sentence, then ask whether they think it would work for them.

line: What kind of work would you like more of next quarter?
followUps: What draws you to that?
What would make room for it?
shareBack: Say what you'd like more of yourself, in a line, then ask how you could help with theirs.
deliveryCue: Good for a 1:1. Follow up on what they say next time.

line: Huge congratulations to the team on this one. Thank you for every late night that went into it.
followUps: Who wants to pick the place for a celebration lunch?
What was the turning point?
shareBack: Thank one person by role for one specific thing, then ask how everyone wants to mark it.
deliveryCue: Swap in what the team pulled off.
